title: Zero-Downtime NOT NULL Constraint Addition on 100-Million Row Tables
realWorldScenario: You need to enforce `NOT NULL` on `orders(customer_id)`. Running `ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id SET NOT NULL;` on a 100-million row table takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock and scans all 100 million rows to verify no NULLs exist, locking out the entire business for 4 minutes.
questionStatement: Explain why traditional `SET NOT NULL` causes database downtime on large tables in PostgreSQL. Detail the 2-step zero-downtime technique using `CHECK ... NOT VALID` followed by `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`. Explain how PostgreSQL 12+ optimizes this pattern.
expectedConcepts: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock held during full table scan in standard SET NOT NULL
CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID instant metadata lock
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT running under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE (concurrent DML allowed)
PostgreSQL 12+ instant promotion from validated check constraint to attnotnull
Dropping redundant check constraint after attnotnull is set
hints: What lock does VALIDATE CONSTRAINT acquire compared to ADD CONSTRAINT?
Does NOT VALID scan existing rows when the constraint is created?
Check how PostgreSQL 12 promotes a validated check constraint to SET NOT NULL.
